title: Spark, Warehouse and the SQL analytics endpoint: where the engine boundary sits
purpose: Spark and Warehouse engine boundary. Shared OneLake Delta storage; Spark engine characteristics; Polaris engine characteristics; SQL analytics endpoint is read only; Where to put which workload.
accessibleSummary: Spark and Warehouse engine boundary. Shared OneLake Delta storage; Spark engine characteristics; Polaris engine characteristics; SQL analytics endpoint is read only; Where to put which workload.
longDescription: Spark and Warehouse engine boundary. Shared OneLake Delta storage; Spark engine characteristics; Polaris engine characteristics; SQL analytics endpoint is read only; Where to put which workload.

nodes.label: Shared OneLake Delta tables
nodes.summary: Both engines operate over the same OneLake Delta tables with no data copy.
nodes.detail: Both engines operate over the same OneLake Delta tables with no data copy.
nodes.whyItMatters: Both engines operate over the same OneLake Delta tables with no data copy.

evidence.note: The Fabric Warehouse and SQL analytics endpoint share one underlying distributed processing architecture with a serverless backend.

processing: Serve the same files to multiple engines
outputs: One physical copy consumed by both engines
drill.example: A table written by Spark is queried by the SQL analytics endpoint without any copy step.
failureModes: Delta protocol upgrades enabled by one engine can make a table unreadable to the other.

nodes.label: Spark — you own the compute shape
nodes.summary: Spark exposes the compute shape and expects you to tune it.
nodes.detail: Spark exposes the compute shape and expects you to tune it.
nodes.whyItMatters: Spark exposes the compute shape and expects you to tune it.

evidence.note: Fabric Spark pools expose node size and autoscale configuration that the user selects.
Native execution offloads supported operators to a vectorized C++ path.

processing: Execute distributed transformation on chosen compute
drill.example: A silver conform job sizes its pool and tunes partitions for its shuffle volume.
failureModes: Performance is your responsibility here — a bad plan or layout is not corrected for you.

nodes.label: Polaris — autonomous, serverless compute
nodes.summary: The Warehouse engine is serverless and autonomous, with no pool to size.
nodes.detail: The Warehouse engine is serverless and autonomous, with no pool to size.
nodes.whyItMatters: The Warehouse engine is serverless and autonomous, with no pool to size.

evidence.note: The SQL frontend optimizes the query and hands the plan to the Distributed Query Processing engine, which splits it into tasks.
Polaris abstracts every dataset as a grid of data cells, making the distributed query processor storage-agnostic.
When the scheduler detects resource pressure it autonomously triggers a scale-out of the backend topology, online.

processing: Compile in the SQL front end
Split into tasks over data cells
outputs: Query results with no user-managed compute
drill.example: A warehouse query scales its backend topology out under load without any pool configuration.
controls: Data modelling and statistics, not compute settings
failureModes: There is no runtime re-optimization equivalent to AQE, so statistics and modelling matter more.

nodes.label: SQL analytics endpoint — read only
nodes.summary: The SQL analytics endpoint is a read-only T-SQL surface over Lakehouse tables.
nodes.detail: The SQL analytics endpoint is a read-only T-SQL surface over Lakehouse tables.
nodes.whyItMatters: The SQL analytics endpoint is a read-only T-SQL surface over Lakehouse tables.

evidence.note: The Warehouse and SQL analytics endpoint share the same underlying architecture.

outputs: Queryable T-SQL objects over the lake
drill.example: An analyst queries lakehouse tables in T-SQL through views without any data movement.
failureModes: Attempting transformation logic here is the most common architectural mistake in Fabric.

nodes.label: Send to Spark
nodes.summary: Transformation, machine learning and gold writes belong in Spark.
nodes.detail: Transformation, machine learning and gold writes belong in Spark.
nodes.whyItMatters: Transformation, machine learning and gold writes belong in Spark.

evidence.note: Writes destined for Direct Lake gold should go through Spark because delta-rs cannot apply V-Order, and distributed shuffles are Spark territory regardless of input size.
V-Order is applied on the write path to optimize reads for Direct Lake and the SQL endpoint.

drill.example: A gold table for Direct Lake is written from Spark so V-Order is applied.
failureModes: Writing gold tables from a non-Spark engine forfeits V-Order optimization.

nodes.label: Send to Warehouse
nodes.summary: T-SQL transformations with multi-table transactions belong in the Warehouse.
nodes.detail: T-SQL transformations with multi-table transactions belong in the Warehouse.
nodes.whyItMatters: T-SQL transformations with multi-table transactions belong in the Warehouse.

evidence.note: The Fabric Warehouse supports transactional writes with autonomous workload management and a serverless backend.

drill.example: A T-SQL team builds marts with stored procedures and multi-table transactions.
failureModes: Compute cannot be tuned, so poor modelling has no configuration remedy.

nodes.label: Send to the endpoint
nodes.summary: BI serving and analyst queries belong on the read-only endpoint.
nodes.detail: BI serving and analyst queries belong on the read-only endpoint.
nodes.whyItMatters: BI serving and analyst queries belong on the read-only endpoint.

evidence.note: The endpoint provides read-only T-SQL over the same Delta files with views and SQL security.

processing: Serve read-only T-SQL over lakehouse tables
outputs: Reports and ad hoc analysis with no data copy
drill.example: Power BI and analysts query the same gold tables Spark just wrote.
failureModes: Deep view chains that recompute on every query should be materialized upstream instead.
